observation_summary: The DateUtils.round() method produces incorrect results for minutes and seconds, failing to round up correctly when the threshold is exceeded.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by incorrect placement of closing braces in the `modify` method of `DateUtils`. In the buggy version, the `if (field == Calendar.SECOND)` and `if (field == Calendar.MINUTE)` checks were nested inside the `if (!round || millisecs < 500)` and `if (!done && (!round || seconds < 30))` blocks respectively. This meant that if the rounding condition (e.g., milliseconds < 500) was false, the code would skip the check to see if it should stop rounding at that field, leading to incorrect truncation or rounding behavior. The fix correctly moves these field checks outside the conditional blocks so that the `done` flag is set regardless of whether the rounding threshold was met.
